newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO chief confirms Castro to attend food summit.
newsitem.headline: FAO chief confirms Castro to attend food summit.

text.p: Cuban leader Fidel Castro will attend a five-day U.N. food summit which opened in Rome on Wednesday, the head of the U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation said on Wednesday.

"He is coming, but I don't know when," FAO director general Jacques Diouf told a reporter, confirming media reports of a planned visit that diplomats say could lead to an historic meeting between Castro and Pope John Paul.
Castro was given a prominent role at the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit on Wednesday when he was named one of the six vice-chairmen for the five-day gathering.
Food Industry Minister Alejandro Roca Iglesias, not Castro, was officially listed as head of the Cuban delegation.
Castro's movements are always cloaked in secrecy. However, diplomatic sources said the 70-year-old communist was expected to arrive in Rome early on Friday.

The Pope is expected to meet Castro later this week, opening the way for his first visit to the Caribbean island whose government has a difficult relationship with the Roman Catholic Church despite recent signs of openness.
